theorem exists_nonzero_targetFixedSpace
    (family : RepresentativeShellFamily)
    (L : MathlibAnnex.CStarAlgebra.PureState.GNSClass Limit →
      MathlibAnnex.CStarAlgebra.PureState.SelectedAtomicHilbert completedRootPureState →L[ℂ]
        MathlibAnnex.CStarAlgebra.PureState.SelectedAtomicHilbert completedRootPureState)
    (hLunit : ∀ i, L i ∈ unitary
      (MathlibAnnex.CStarAlgebra.PureState.SelectedAtomicHilbert completedRootPureState →L[ℂ]
        MathlibAnnex.CStarAlgebra.PureState.SelectedAtomicHilbert completedRootPureState))
    (hLsource : ∀ i n, (L i).comp (selectedAtomicRepresentation
      (transportedFlag family i n - transportedFlag family i (n + 1))) =
        representedShellLink family i n)
    {K : Type v} [NormedAddCommGroup K] [InnerProductSpace ℂ K]
    [CompleteSpace K] (rho : Representation (AtomicTarget L) K)
    (hrho : rho.IsIrreducible) :
    ∃ i : MathlibAnnex.CStarAlgebra.PureState.GNSClass Limit,
      (⨅ n, ((restrictedRepresentation L rho)
        (transportedFlag family i n)).range) ≠ ⊥

content.assumptions:
Let $A$ be the completed CAR algebra, obtained by completing the matrix stages $M_{2^n}(\mathbb C)$ with embeddings $a\mapsto a\otimes I_2$. Let $f_n$ be the image of the first diagonal matrix unit. Thus $f_0=1$ and the $f_n$ form a decreasing sequence of projections. The root state $\omega$ has value $a_{00}$ on a matrix $a$ in any stage.

Choose a pure state $\varphi_j$ in each unitary-equivalence class $j\in I$ of pure-state GNS representations, with $\varphi_o=\omega$ at the root index $o$. Denote its complete complex GNS space, unital star representation and unit cyclic vector by $(H_j,\pi_j,\xi_j)$. Set $\mathcal H=\bigoplus_{j\in I}H_j$ and $\pi=\bigoplus_{j\in I}\pi_j$. The index set need not be countable.

A supplied shell family consists of unital complex star automorphisms $\alpha_j$ with $\varphi_j\circ\alpha_j=\omega$ and elements $w_{j,n}\in A$. Put $f_{j,n}=\alpha_j(f_n)$. Their support identities are $w_{j,n}^*w_{j,n}=f_{j,n}-f_{j,n+1}$ and $w_{j,n}w_{j,n}^*=f_n-f_{n+1}$. At the root, $\alpha_o$ is the identity and $w_{o,n}=f_n-f_{n+1}$.

Let $L_j$ be unitaries on $\mathcal H$ satisfying $L_j\pi(f_{j,n}-f_{j,n+1})=\pi(w_{j,n})$ for every $j,n$. Let $T\subseteq B(\mathcal H)$ be the norm-closed unital star algebra generated by $\pi(A)$ and all $L_j$. Write $\iota:A\to T$ for $\iota(a)=\pi(a)$ and $g_j\in T$ for the element represented by $L_j$. For a unital complex star representation $\rho:T\to B(K)$ on a complete complex Hilbert space, put $\sigma=\rho\circ\iota$ and $V_j=\rho(g_j)$. Each $V_j$ is unitary because $\rho$ preserves the unit, products and adjoints. Here irreducibility includes nonzero representation and means that the only closed subspaces invariant under every represented operator and its adjoint are $\{0\}$ and $K$. No root normalization $L_o=I$ or prescribed transport of the atomic cyclic vectors is assumed.
content.conclusion: At least one transported flag retains a nonzero common fixed vector. This supplies the initial vector for the residual-corner construction of vector states. The assertion concerns existence of some $i$; it neither chooses a distinguished index nor says that this common range is one-dimensional.
content.display_title: An irreducible target representation has a surviving fixed space
content.lean_realization_notes: The temporary assertion that $\sigma$ is irreducible occurs inside the contradiction argument under the all-zero hypothesis. It is not asserted for every source restriction. Strong limits are taken on $K$, while extension from source and generators to $T$ uses norm-closed generation.
content.natural_language_statement: For the shell family and generated algebra described below, let $\rho:T\to B(K)$ be a nonzero irreducible unital star representation and put $\sigma=\rho\circ\iota$. Then there is an index $i\in I$ such that $F_i=\bigcap_{n\geq0}\operatorname{ran}\sigma(f_{i,n})$ is nonzero.
content.one_sentence_role: Rules out simultaneous disappearance of all limiting CAR flags by passing reduction through the reconstructed generators.

proof_steps.text: Let $M\subseteq K$ be a closed subspace reducing $\sigma$. Every $\sigma(w_{i,n})$ and its adjoint preserve $M$, hence so do their finite sums. Closure of $M$ passes this invariance to the two strong limits $S_i$ and $S_i^*$. Under $F_i=\{0\}$, the formula $R_i=V_iP_i$ gives $R_i=0$, so $M$ reduces $V_i$.

The orthogonal projection onto $M$ commutes with the represented source and all added generators. Its commutation relation persists under algebraic star operations and norm limits. Consequently $M$ reduces every $\rho(t)$, $t\in T$, and irreducibility of $\rho$ forces $M=\{0\}$ or $K$. The space $K$ is nonzero and $\sigma$ is unital, so this proves nonzero irreducibility of $\sigma$ under the supposition.

Coverage by selected pure-state GNS representations supplies an index $j$ and a unitary $e:K\to H_j$ with $e\sigma(a)=\pi_j(a)e$ for every $a\in A$. The vector $\eta=e^{-1}\xi_j$ has norm one. Since $\varphi_j(f_{j,n})=\omega(f_n)=1$, each projection $\pi_j(f_{j,n})$ fixes $\xi_j$; intertwining therefore gives $\sigma(f_{j,n})\eta=\eta$ for all $n$.
A fixed vector of a projection belongs to its range. Thus $\eta\in F_j$, contradicting $F_j=\{0\}$ and $\|\eta\|=1$. This completes the exclusion of the all-zero case.

content.proof_summary: Suppose all $F_i$ vanish, and write $P_i$ for the orthogonal projection onto $F_i$. Let $S_i$ be the strong sum of the represented shell links. By the [shell reconstruction theorem](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/CAR/TargetReconstruction.lean#L121-L178), in each reconstructed generator $V_i=S_i+R_i$, the initial residual projection is zero, so $R_i=0$. Every closed reducing subspace for $\sigma$ therefore reduces every $V_i$, and hence the entire target representation. Thus $\sigma$ would be irreducible. [Coverage by selected pure-state GNS representations](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/PureStateGNS/IrreduciblePure.lean#L212-L232) then transports a selected cyclic vector back to a nonzero vector fixed by one of the flags, contradicting the assumption.

citations.label: The root state bundled with its purity proof

guide: Here `Limit` is $A$, [`completedRootPureState`](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/CAR/CompletedSource.lean#L16-L18) is the root state $\omega$ bundled with its purity proof, and `SelectedAtomicHilbert completedRootPureState` is the atomic Hilbert space $\mathcal H$. `hrho : rho.IsIrreducible` includes nonzero irreducibility of $\rho$. The expression `⨅ n, ... .range` is $F_i$, and `≠ ⊥` means that this subspace is not $\{0\}$. `restrictedRepresentation L rho` is $\sigma$; the source conclusion quantifies over an index `i` and does not claim irreducibility of $\sigma$ without the temporary all-zero hypothesis used in the proof.
